reason: Part (a) cannot be implemented because the thing it would change does not exist. predict_unet_transformer.py runs 2-frame windows with no padding (confirmed by research). Part (b) is easy to build (per-component t0/t1 in filter_short_track_components) and can be replayed in the lab, but research measured it at about break-even: per side, +0.00045 from edges and -0.00055 from the node multiplier. The ILP clip-end exemption, which is the corrected mechanism, is a one-line patch at predict script L561-566. I checked it on tracksdata 0.1.0rc9 with a toy 4-node chain at p=0.6: the default a0/d2 selects 0 nodes, and pl.when(t==T_LAST) with disappearance 0.05 plus appearance -1 at t0 selects all 4. The NodeAttr comparison form also works. So writing the code is not the problem. Testing and value are. (1) The ILP variant cannot be replayed. Friend A's cache has raw/ (ILP solution only), ckpt, dc and divnet, and no pre-ILP candidate graph is stored anywhere. A full GPU pipeline pass is needed at about 2.5 min/video (CONTEXT L958): about 2.7 GPU-h for SELECTION (64 videos) and about 5.6 GPU-h for CONFIRMATION (135 videos). That is 40% of the ~20 GPU-h left, competing with the coordinate-head port and its retraining, which have the largest known LB lever. Research estimated 0.5-1 GPU-h, which is too low. A SCIP re-solve must also reproduce friend A's raw/ node-for-node for the control. (2) There is a structural no-op against the short-track filter. The ILP pays the end cost wherever a track ends, so it would already have extended any track ending at t96 into t97-99 if a candidate edge existed. The nodes it drops at the clip ends are therefore isolated new segments of at most 3 nodes (start at t>=97 or end at t<=2). OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN=6 and SHORT_TRACK_RESCUE_MIN_LEN=4 delete them, and weak-leaf pruning 0.3 plus the edge filter also go after low- or zero-p relink edges. The ILP fix alone changes nothing in the output. It only has an effect together with a K<=3 tail exemption, and that exemption is almost pure node cost: about 12.6k nodes at about 0.009 TP edges/node vs 0.061 for an average node. (3) The value is below the protocol by construction. The oracle ceiling is +0.0011 local (all 154 excess boundary FN, at zero cost), under the +0.002 gate before the roughly 0.3% node multiplier (about -0.0003). Expected public gain is 0 to +0.0003, below the ±0.003 LB noise floor, so a probe could not detect it. With 5 days and 5 probes/day committed elsewhere (exp51 coordhead, probes 29/30), it cannot pass the gate or be verified on the LB.
fix_if_any: Drop part (a) and do not run the tail-only grid, whose predicted result is about 0. Keep the ILP clip-end exemption only as a free rider. If a GPU run that dumps the pre-ILP candidate graph happens anyway (e.g. the coordhead capture/retraining pass on 199 videos, or a B9 ILP-calibration dump), add save_graph(graph) before solver.solve at L561 in that run. Then re-solve on a Kaggle CPU kernel with disappearance = pl.when(pl.col('t')==T_LAST).then(C_END).otherwise(2.0) and appearance = pl.when(pl.col('t')==0).then(-B_START).otherwise(0.0). Take T_LAST from the image frame count, not the max node t. Pair it with a clip-end tail exemption, K_START/K_END in {3,4}, applied only to components with mean edge_prob >= 0.7. First check that the restored segments survive leaf-prune and the edge filter. Accept it only if it passes the standard gate, which the ceiling makes unlikely. Otherwise spend no GPU or probe budget on it.
realistic_public_gain: About 0 (0 to +0.0003), undetectable against the ±0.003 LB noise. Local oracle ceiling +0.0011, realistic 0 to +0.0005 local.
